text:
Priya K: Spike: interruptible-enqueue pattern for continuous batcher — short writeup + tradeoffs. TL;DR: mark some requests as interruptible; if they would extend current window beyond latency SLO we move them into an interruptible holding queue that can be resumed or served as its own microbatch. Advantages: prevents head-of-line small requests from being delayed by long requests while keeping high throughput. Drawbacks: complexity around KV cache and fairness. Posting examples + config. Feedback?
Dan R: How is this different from soft-preempt lanes we discussed? sounds like demotion rather than preempt.
Priya K: Yeah similar surface, but key difference: instead of preempting running tokens we prevent enqueue commit for candidate requests. So no K/V rollbacks. Preempt was evicting partially processed batches; this avoids that.
Mike L: Concern: can this starve large batches? if we keep demoting long jobs, we might never finish high-throughput work.
Priya K: We can add a 'demotion_budget' per tenant + an aging bump that promotes after X ms. Also track demotion_count metric.
Eva S: KV cache: if we demote before the model's kv warm-up, you'll get separate KV states and worse perf. How do we avoid duplicating cache fills?
Priya K: Option A: allow demoted requests to hold a 'cache-reservation' token that keeps KV entries pinned but doesn't consume compute slots. Option B: give demoted requests a chance to re-join soon with affinity to same shard. Both have tradeoffs.
Dan R: Pinning KV entries seems memory heavy. What's cost on p50/p99 workload for LLM-13B?
Priya K: Estimate: each session kv ~ 1.2MB for 13B per active beam. Pinning for N=50 add ~60MB per GPU. Acceptable in many tails but not for dense multitenant.
Mike L: We should try a prototype without pinning first. Maybe use short TTL on pinned entries and metrics to watch kv_hit_rate.
Priya K: Agreed. Proto config snippet:
```yaml
queue:
  mode: continuous
  interruptible:
    enabled: true
    demotion_budget_per_minute: 20
    aging_promotion_ms: 250
    reserve_kv_when_demoted: false
```
Eva S: Need to expose telemetry: demotion_rate, demoted_rejoin_latency, kv_dup_rate, tenant_starvation_alert. Add SLO for tail tokens.
Priya K: I'll wire metrics to per-tenant dashboards. Also thought about admission: if interruptible queue grows > X we fall back to fallback model (smaller) automatically.
Dan R: @Priya can you note the API change? probably just annotation on request: { interruptible: bool } so client can opt-in.
Priya K: Yes. Default false for backward compat. We'll gate via feature flag.
Mike L: :thumbsup: I can run a few perf sims on the trace replay infra.
deploy-bot: perf-sim job #884 enqueued by Mike L — status: queued
Priya K: One more edge: interactions with streaming. Streaming requests can't easily be demoted mid-stream. We'll treat initial token generation as atomic: if streaming flag set, interruptible must be false.
Eva S: Good call. Also add a note: demoted requests should gain a 'fastpath' if their rejoin happens within X ms to avoid double-penalty.
Dan R: Ok I'm good with prototype. Sketch a follow-up RFC: interface, telemetry, KV options, fairness knobs. assign to Priya + Mike.
Priya K: Will do. I'll drop a short RFC draft later today. Thanks y'all :rocket:
